scope: Tranche 1 (a) — AppImage discovery in the Zig backend, and the defects it exposed
delivered: appimage/discovery.zig: scans the installation directory, correlates the XDG desktop entries, merges into the database without degrading any record.
AppImageManager.discoverAppImages(): the backend reads its own directory; the Python engine no longer writes a file it does not own.
shelly sync appimage --discover: the scan alone, without the metadata refresh.
defects_fixed: copyFile did not preserve the mode; a rename during the sync dropped the AppImage's executable bit.

Upstream's commits past v3.1.8 removed the setExecutable call that repaired it; the metadata extraction runs the AppImage, so spawn returned AccessDenied and aborted the whole synchronisation. Both restored.
The sync renamed a file without touching the desktop entries that referenced it, leaving twenty broken menu entries. The backend now clears them, as it already did on install and removal.
Seventeen AppImage test sites ran with the real process environment and wrote into the user's own ~/.local/share/applications. They now use an environment rooted in a temporary directory.
The Python engine listed X-AppImage-Name among the version keys, so the openwork AppImage reported its version as "OpenWork" instead of "0.18.42".
known_gaps: The AppImage backend still renames files to <Name>.AppImage during a sync, which changes the vendor's desktop entries. The backend now clears the stale ones, but the crafts launcher may recreate its own entries with the old paths on its next run.
Discovery reads the desktop entries; the version in the database is still refreshed by the metadata extraction, which runs the AppImage binary.
